texts: good. the "in deep winter" restriction goes into a season-conditioned property atom, so nothing claims thin moth-counts year-round.
good. the bare-plural generic becomes a fireable distributing rule at generic strength, with the season carried on the derived event.
good. the seasonal restriction rides the condition slot rather than being stripped, so no unrestricted "moth-counts are strong" is asserted.

bad: the parse asserts a single flat peaking event with the bare kind word in the role slot, rather than the yearly regularity you mean — and the licensed generic form would say each individual count peaks, which is not what a peak is (it is a property of the series, not of one count). Give the series a definite bearer so it can hold the predicate: "The moth-count peaks in early autumn."

bad: same shape as the peak sentence — a single flat decline event with the bare kind "moth-count" in the role slot and at individual-fact confidence, instead of the seasonal regularity. Your "Moth-counts recover through spring" parsed correctly in exactly this wording, so the sentence is not really at fault, but the definite-series form is the more robust phrasing: "The moth-count declines through late autumn."
